description:
Why: several examples have a crossover (ws_masking: 1 KiB; codecs, Snappy, per-call SAT) below which the optimised Elixir is as fast or faster than the kernel. A caller can switch by data today with one function clause, but no guide shows it. Discussed after the verdict (defk-sgw.6, 2026-10-14): no automatic switch in defk; document the user-side pattern.

Note: the crossover in Defk.Bench is 'first size where defk is >= 2x the optimised Elixir', not the break-even point, and the fast Elixir below it is the hand-written baseline (often another algorithm or a BIF), not the kernel's Elixir mode.

Scope:
1. A section in docs/guides/measuring.md (or getting-started.md, whichever reads better): a guard clause such as
   def mask(frame) when byte_size(frame) < 1024, do: mask_elixir(frame)
   def mask(frame), do: Kernels.mask(frame)
   How to pick the threshold (a sweep on the target machine, a wide margin, thresholds move with machine and load), and that the Elixir clause needs an agreement test against the kernel (Defk.Test.assert_agrees or a property over both functions).
2. Point at ws_masking as the worked case.
3. HexDocs page: no ticket or ADR references (user-facing extra).

Done when: the section exists, its code example runs in the docs checks, and mix ci is green.

title: Guide: call a kernel only above a size, with an Elixir clause below it
